title: Narrow and log the catch-all in CompletionRepositoryImpl._appendStreakEvent

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // Defensive: never let a telemetry tee block the primary write.

why: catch (_) swallows every exception from BOTH the streak_events Drift insert and the outbox enqueue (facade.enqueueStreakPayload) with no AppLogger call anywhere in this file — a codec bug, closed-DB race, or genuine corruption is indistinguishable from the expected benign duplicate-key case this comment is defending against. This is also EH-4-adjacent (catches Error subtypes, not just typed Exceptions) and evades the Rule-0 'no empty catch blocks' Makefile grep (`catch\s*(_\?\w*)\s*{}`), which only matches a literal same-line `{}` — this multi-line comment-only body is functionally empty but textually invisible to that checker. Per the file's own header comment, the outbox enqueue here is what 'closes the gap' where a second device sees a frozen streak; if enqueueStreakPayload throws, that gap silently reopens with zero diagnostic trail and no retry.
recommendation: Catch a specific expected type (e.g. the Drift unique-constraint exception) for the benign-duplicate case and let everything else propagate or be logged via AppLogger.instance.warning/error before swallowing, so a genuine failure is at least visible in Crashlytics/Talker.
acceptance_criteria: The catch narrows to the specific expected exception type; every other path logs via AppLogger before returning; a regression test that makes enqueueStreakPayload throw asserts the failure is logged, not silently dropped.

corrections: The cited 'closes the gap' comment is the doc-comment immediately above _appendStreakEvent (~line 727), not the file's top header — minor mislabel, doesn't affect the claim's substance since it's in the same file and directly tied to the cited catch block.
